Prepare a Standard Visit Table

Source: R/prep_visits.R
prep_visits.Rd

Convert raw NEDAP or FIRE station data into a standard visit table with the same columns and units for both station types.

prep_visits(data, station = NULL, qc = qc_config(), verbose = 1)

Arguments

data

Raw station data, e.g. from read_station() or the example datasets nedap and fire.

station

"nedap", "fire" or NULL (default): taken from the "station" attribute set by read_station(), or detected from the column names.

qc

QC settings from qc_config(). Used here: duration_max (to tell a FIRE midnight crossing from a recording error) and the station transfer parameters max_gap_days, max_overlap_days, max_jump_kg.

verbose

0 (silent), 1 (summary, default) or 2 (details).

Value

A data.table, one row per visit, ordered by location and entry_time:

  • responder: pig ID (character, NA for unidentified visits); responder_raw: transponder number as recorded;

  • breed: kept when the input has a breed column; otherwise add it with add_breed();

  • identified: FALSE for visits without a transponder read;

  • location: station (feeder) ID, character;

  • date, seq_days (day number from the first day in the data, 1 = first day), seq_in_day (visit number of the pig that day), seq_in_location (visit number on the feeder that day);

  • entry_time, exit_time: POSIXct, UTC; duration: seconds;

  • feed_intake: g; weight: body weight, kg (NA if not recorded);

  • trough_in, trough_out: trough weight at entrance and exit, g (FIRE only, NA for NEDAP); topup: feed dispensed, g (FIRE only);

  • source_file, if present in the input.

Attributes:

  • "station": station type;

  • "stations": one row per pig with its station history (see below);

  • "removed": log of visits removed as transponder misreads;

  • "prep_summary": number of rows dropped at each step.

Station transfer

For each pig seen at several stations, the time span at each station is compared:

  • misread: the span at a minor station overlaps the span at the main station (most visits) by more than max_overlap_days. Visits at the minor station inside the main span are removed as transponder misreads.

  • transfer: consecutive spans are separated by at most max_gap_days. All visits are kept, each with its real location. A body weight jump above max_jump_kg at the transfer gives a warning.

  • split: a gap longer than max_gap_days. The spans are treated as different animals and responder becomes "<id>_<location>".

A pig that returns to a station it already used is not supported: the return looks like an overlap and is treated as misreads.

See also

read_station() for the previous step.

Examples

visits <- prep_visits(fire)
#> 
#> ── Preparing FIRE visits ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> • Visits read: 9,794
#> • Unidentified visits (kept, identified = FALSE): 51
#> • FIRE visits crossing midnight (exit time corrected): 68
#> • Body weights of 0 set to NA: 478
#> • Rows without entry time (dropped): 0
#> • Duplicated rows (dropped): 0
#> ℹ No pig was seen at more than one station
#> ✔ 26 pigs at 2 stations, 9794 visits over 66 days
#> ℹ No breed column. To use breed in the feed intake model and breed-specific limits, add it with `add_breed()`.
head(visits)
#>    responder responder_raw identified location       date seq_days seq_in_day
#>       <char>        <char>     <lgcl>   <char>     <Date>    <int>      <int>
#> 1:     35877         35877       TRUE      101 2023-12-19        1          1
#> 2:     35873         35873       TRUE      101 2023-12-19        1          1
#> 3:     35878         35878       TRUE      101 2023-12-19        1          1
#> 4:     35855         35855       TRUE      101 2023-12-19        1          1
#> 5:     35877         35877       TRUE      101 2023-12-19        1          2
#> 6:     35853         35853       TRUE      101 2023-12-19        1          1
#>    seq_in_location          entry_time           exit_time duration feed_intake
#>              <int>              <POSc>              <POSc>    <num>       <num>
#> 1:               1 2023-12-19 14:15:39 2023-12-19 14:18:02      143          46
#> 2:               2 2023-12-19 14:18:03 2023-12-19 14:23:05      302         248
#> 3:               3 2023-12-19 14:23:15 2023-12-19 14:28:45      330         201
#> 4:               4 2023-12-19 14:29:05 2023-12-19 14:34:29      324         121
#> 5:               5 2023-12-19 14:34:30 2023-12-19 14:34:37        7           0
#> 6:               6 2023-12-19 14:34:38 2023-12-19 14:36:26      108           0
#>    weight trough_in trough_out topup
#>     <num>     <num>      <num> <num>
#> 1:   67.6       678        632   286
#> 2:   60.8       632        384     0
#> 3:   70.8       670        469   286
#> 4:   51.2       755        634   286

#> 6:   88.6       634        634     0

# Unidentified visits are kept for the feeder error checks
table(visits$identified)
#> 
#> FALSE  TRUE 
#>    51  9743 

# Station history of each pig
head(attr(visits, "stations"))
#>    responder responder_raw location_path main_location n_locations transfer
#>       <char>        <char>        <char>        <char>       <int>   <lgcl>
#> 1:     25822         25822           101           101           1    FALSE
#> 2:     35853         35853           101           101           1    FALSE
#> 3:     35855         35855           101           101           1    FALSE
#> 4:     35862         35862           101           101           1    FALSE
#> 5:     35865         35865           101           101           1    FALSE
#> 6:     35869         35869           101           101           1    FALSE
#>     split misreads_removed weight_jump_kg
#>    <lgcl>            <int>          <num>
#> 1:  FALSE                0             NA
#> 2:  FALSE                0             NA
#> 3:  FALSE                0             NA
#> 4:  FALSE                0             NA
#> 5:  FALSE                0             NA
#> 6:  FALSE                0             NA

# NEDAP data gets the same columns and units
nedap_visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
summary(nedap_visits$weight)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.     NAs 
#>   20.50   43.00   80.00   77.17  106.50  147.75     391
